blocks.heading: Questions Before You Commit to This Path

items.text: A single salary figure, or one relative's opinion about "coding being a safe bet," cannot tell you whether this path genuinely fits your specific situation.
Can you sit through long, focused debugging sessions without burning out, and stay comfortable with the field asking you to keep relearning tools every couple of years.
Web development rewards sustained focus and comfort with continuous, low-drama change more than raw intensity in short bursts.

The options below lead with the ones that carry the strongest real growth headroom today, infrastructure ownership and product decision-making both tend to keep scaling in pay and scope well past what a generalist coding skill alone commands, rather than a random or conventional order.
DevOps or cloud infrastructure, if you found deployment and systems reliability more interesting than feature-building
A related but distinct specialisation focused on how applications run and scale in production, commanding a genuine premium and sitting further from routine AI-automatable coding work.

blocks.heading: Avoid When Deciding on Web Development

items.text: Course-completion alone rarely convinces an employer.
Shallow familiarity across many tools competes for less differentiated, more AI-exposed roles than genuine depth in one lane.
Developers who treat AI tools as an unfair shortcut to avoid, rather than a skill to learn to use well, are choosing to be less efficient than peers who have integrated them into a real workflow.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Real pay by stack and experience

rows: Fresher web developer, 0-1 years
Rs 3.5-6 LPA
Service companies and smaller product startups sit at the lower end; a genuinely strong portfolio of shipped projects can push a fresher toward the upper end even without prior work experience.
Mid-level developer, 2-4 years
Rs 7-14 LPA
The widest band in the field, driven far more by depth in a specific stack and system-design ability than by years alone at this stage.
Senior developer, 5-8 years
Rs 16-30 LPA
Requires genuine ownership of architecture decisions, not just feature delivery, the jump from mid-level to senior is a skill jump, not a tenure milestone.
Staff/lead engineer or engineering manager, 8+ years
Rs 30-55 LPA and above

Concentrated at product companies, well-funded startups, and global capability centres, this tier requires either deep technical leadership or people-management ability layered on top of engineering skill.
Freelance/contract web development, project-based
Rs 500-3,000+ per hour depending on stack, client geography, and specialisation
A genuinely scalable income lane for developers with a track record and a specific in-demand skill, but income is inconsistent without deliberate client-pipeline building, unlike a salaried role.

blocks.heading: Think Twice Before Choosing Web Development
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Who should think twice before choosing web development

rows: You are entering web development assuming junior roles are as plentiful as they were five years ago
AI coding tools have genuinely reduced demand for developers who only do narrow, boilerplate junior work. Entry now rewards a real portfolio and some depth, not just course completion certificates.
You dislike continuous learning and want a stack you master once and use unchanged for a decade
Web development tooling and best practices shift meaningfully every few years. A developer uncomfortable with ongoing relearning will feel a real, recurring friction in this field specifically.
You are choosing "full-stack" by default because it sounds safer than picking a lane

Genuine full-stack depth takes longer to build than surface-level full-stack familiarity. A shallow full-stack profile competes for less differentiated roles than a genuinely deep frontend or backend specialist.
You are treating AI-panic headlines as a reason to avoid the field entirely

The realistic picture is bifurcation, not collapse, routine boilerplate work is genuinely shrinking, while system design, debugging, and AI-tool direction are growing in value. The field is not disappearing; the floor for what counts as valuable work is rising.

visuals.heading: Pick a Lane Before Researching Further

items.text: Frontend development (React, Vue, or similar) builds what users actually see and click, layout, interactivity, performance in the browser.
Backend development builds what users never see, servers, databases, APIs, business logic.

Full-stack developers work across both, trading some depth in either for broader project ownership, genuinely useful at smaller companies and startups, less differentiated at large product companies with dedicated specialist teams.

blocks.heading: What AI Is Actually Replacing Here

items.text: AI coding assistants now write a substantial share of routine boilerplate, CRUD forms, basic component scaffolding, common API integration patterns, straightforward styling, genuinely faster than a human typing it manually.
Entry-level hiring at some companies has become more selective specifically because AI tools now cover a meaningful slice of what juniors used to be hired to do.

blocks.heading: Not a Flat Yes or No

items.text: You have picked, or are close to picking, a specific lane, frontend, backend, or a genuine full-stack depth, rather than staying generically unspecialised.
You are comfortable with continuous learning as a normal, ongoing part of the job, not an occasional inconvenience.
You have, or are actively building, a real portfolio of deployed, working projects, not just completed course certificates.
